Hello fellow scientist! You sound fed up and a little lost. That's okay, that's me every Wednesday. But, I am curious as to why you equate your core values with your beliefs? I personally don't think those are the same thing. Perhaps this is a poor example but I strongly believe in working hard, but wow do I value my down time - so much so that I always make sure that I get it, even if I need to schedule it into a busy day.

How much do you usually shake up your life? I'm all for changing things up, especially if I'm not happy, but there's a lot to be said for some stability as well. For example, change where you live but keep your job, or visa versa. Those are large changes though. Depending on what exactly it is you are tired off, shaking up your weekly routine may give you a little perk up and allow you some clearer headspace to assess your current situation.

getting a middle class job, accepting that reality by trapping yourself with a family and grinding a job for three decades

There is no rule stating that you need to do this. At all. I absolutely love my job. Can I see myself doing it until I retire? Eh, no. I would get bored. Are there things that I do as hobbies that I could make money from, should I choose to? Yes. My interests are very varied so I don't get bored with anything really, and even though I can't currently picture myself starting a business, who knows what I'll want to do in the future? I certainly don't :D

Success is a very subjective thing. For one person it could be becoming a CEO of a large company. For others it could be as simple as doing something that is out of their comfort zone. My rule of thumb is to define success as happiness. If your decisions lead you down a path that make you happy, go for it. Don't put yourself in a difficult position (eg, financially) to "go for it" as that will impact your future success (happiness). Being a logical person, you'll likely know that already, and be unlikely to "shake things up" to your own detriment. Don't take that greater gamble until you've cleared your head, stepped back and assessed your position as best you can. Quickly leaving a life you're fed up of is not a good enough reason to jump ship into unknown territory. Put your (fed up) feelings aside and make an unbiased judgement, based on the facts you have and any other facts you can obtain. Go all scientist on its ass.

Family is also a subjective term. Your friends may be focusing on children, which doesn't sound like something that interests you, but that doesn't mean that you don't have family. Even if you don't have parents/siblings/cousins, there is a network of people in your life who you value and you can consider them your family. Make sure to keep in touch with them, even if you have to listen to a few baby stories before you get to the regular stuff. If they have children, it may slip their mind, or be more difficult to pick up the phone first, but those babies will grow up and it would be a shame to lose touch before your friends have their time to themselves again.

A big satisfaction many parents get is a feeling of being needed, and having a purpose. It is some people's way of filling up a hollow feeling. I'm not suggesting that you have a child (!) but maybe look for something to do that depends on you, like volunteering at a fixed time during the week. Or something. I don't know. Anything that relies on you. I specifically stayed away from the pet example because I don't know you or your situation, but I get great pleasure from canine companions ;)

These were all random generic suggestions. And I apologize for that. If I knew you I'd offer a chat over coffee to vent out all your frustrations. I hope you have someone in your life you can suggest that to.

TL;DR: you are not trapped. You do not have to have a conventional job or lifestyle from now until you die. Go be interesting and go be happy - but make sensible choices along the way. Best of luck.
